basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A typed, directed link between organizations, not either organization's identity.
Keeps affiliation, supply, consolidation and ownership as different kinds that cannot be read as one another.
Distinguishes the real-world relation, the publisher's record and an observer's claim.
Differs from a contract: a relationship may rest on a contract but is not its execution.

may: Resolve a relationship and its participants for a stated time.
Traverse asserted links and clearly label any derived ones.
Record an attributed assertion or counterclaim with its source.
Export a permitted projection of the relationship graph.
mustNot: Infer control, beneficial ownership or legal authority from a generic link.
Treat an unreported relationship as proof that none exists.
Merge parallel relationships between the same parties into one.
Use a relationship record to authorize a transaction or signature.
requiresHuman: Publishing ownership or control conclusions about organizations.

considerations: Ownership chains can reveal natural persons behind organizations, which raises privacy and safety issues.
False affiliation links can damage reputations or trigger sanctions screening errors.
Transparency of ownership serves anti-corruption goals and should not be lost in projections.
affectedParties: Beneficial owners and officers behind them
Regulators, investors and journalists who rely on the graph

items: A relationship has two or more participant references, a kind, a direction, a validity period and a source.
Confused with the organizations themselves, a contract, a transaction and a consolidated group.
False sanctions or compliance hits from wrong ownership links.
Hidden control when withheld links are treated as absent.
Graph loops and inflated influence from derived links.
GLEIF Level 2 relationship records with LEI, ISO 17442.
Beneficial Ownership Data Standard from Open Ownership.
